ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, $ \angle C=90^\circ$, AD bisects $ \angle BAC$, $ DE\perp AB$ with foot E, $ AB=12$, $ AC=8$, what is the length of BE?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ AD bisects $\angle$BAC,\\
$\therefore$$\angle$DAE=$\angle$DAC\\
$\because$$\angle$C=90$^\circ$, DE$\perp$AB,\\
$\therefore$$\angle$AED=$\angle$ACD=90$^\circ$,\\
Also, AD=AD,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$ADE$\cong$ $\triangle$ADC,\\
$\therefore$AE=AC,\\
$\because$AB=12, AC=8,\\
$\therefore$BE=AB−AE=AB−AC=12−8=\boxed{4}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is right triangle ABC, A is at the upper right, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, AC is vertical, BC is horizontal, and there is a right-angle mark at C. D is located on BC, and AD is connected. E is located on AB, and DE is connected, and there is a right-angle mark at E, indicating that DE is perpendicular to AB. Reasoning: Because AD bisects ∠BAC, and E is on AB, ∠DAE = ∠DAC. Also because DE ⟂ AB, ∠AED = 90°; the figure and the problem statement give ∠C = 90°, and D is on BC, so ∠ACD = 90°. The two right triangles ADE and ADC share hypotenuse AD, and have a pair of equal acute angles at A, therefore triangle ADE congruent to triangle ADC. Thus AE = AC = 8. Since E is on AB and AB = 12, BE = AB - AE = 12 - 8 = 4.
